findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body: After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still call the disposed handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles retain listeners and cause duplicate callbacks and growing resource use.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned teardown
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, any later `"message"` event still invokes the supposedly detached handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and stale callbacks after disposal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the function returned by `attach()` no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any socket emitting after disposal still invokes the handler, causing stale callbacks and accumulating duplicate listeners across reattachments.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
For any socket whose `on` method retains listeners, calling `attach`, invoking its returned cleanup, and keeping the socket alive leaves `handler` registered. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles therefore retain handlers indefinitely and make every later message invoke all disposed handlers, causing unbounded memory use and callback work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
